newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Sept wholesale inventories fell 1.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Sept wholesale inventories fell 1.3 pct.

text.p: Commerce Department report of wholesale inventories and sales, seasonally adjusted.
(Billions of dollars) Sept Aug--Rev from Sept'95
Wall Street economists had expected a 0.3 percent rise in September wholesale inventories.
The 1.3 percent drop in September wholesale inventories was the biggest for any month in 14-1/2 years, since February 1982 when stocks of unsold goods dropped 1.6 percent, the department said.

The stock-to-sales ratio for merchant wholesalers, seasonally adjusted, fell to 1.27 months' worth in September from a revised 1.29 months' worth in August that was previously reported as 1.30 months.
The department said it was the lowest stock-to-sales ratio since August 1990 when it also was at 1.27 months' worth.
The ratio is a measure of how many months it would take to sell existing inventories at the current sales pace.
